mainTopic: Feeding one's children: readings of the משנה, the תקנות of אושא, and how they were enforced
overview: The גמרא first finishes matching our משנה ('a father is not obligated to feed his daughter') to רבי מאיר. It then offers two more readings, by רבי יהודה and by רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא. Next it brings a תקנה made in אושא: a man must feed his young sons and daughters. Stories about רב יהודה, רב חסדא and רבא show that judges only shamed such a father and did not force him. The exception is a wealthy father, whom the court does force, just as רבא forced רב נתן בר אמי to give charity. A second אושא rule follows: a man who gives all his property to his sons is still fed from it, together with his wife. The גמרא asks why that rule was needed when a widow is fed even after the property passed to the daughter's husband. It answers that a living husband might have been told to go work. Finally the גמרא asks whether the הלכה follows this rule and begins a story about רבי יונתן, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the רבי מאיר reading: no duty for a daughter, but still a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: This line ends the reading of the משנה according to רבי מאיר. The משנה mentions 'daughter' to teach that even for her there is no legal duty, though there is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentions his daughter to teach that even for his daughter there is no obligation, but there is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its first answer, that our משנה follows רבי מאיר. It explains why the משנה chose to mention the daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that feeding daughters is a מצוה, and feeding sons is a מצוה all the more so (קל וחומר). The משנה says 'not obligated' about the daughter to show that even for her it is only a מצוה, not a חובה. So for the son it is certainly not a חובה either.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal obligation that בית דין can enforce
A good deed one should do, but not one that can be forced

steps.confusionAlert: Saying 'not obligated' does not mean 'not good to do.' The whole סוגיא depends on the gap between חובה (enforceable duty) and מצוה (a good deed).

phrases.english: That even his daughter,
it is an obligation that there is not,
but a מצוה there is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading by רבי מאיר that began before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Matching the משנה to a תנא and explaining its wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Why would the משנה mention the daughter if the son is the easier case?
steps.terutzMaskana: Mentioning the daughter shows that even for her there is only a מצוה, not a חובה

steps.title: Second reading: the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can also follow רבי יהודה, who holds that feeding sons is a מצוה and feeding daughters is one all the more so. The משנה mentions the daughter to teach that even for her there is no legal duty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say the משנה follows רבי יהודה. Read it this way: a father is not obligated to feed his daughter, and all the more so not his son. There is a מצוה for a son, and all the more so for daughters. The משנה mentions the daughter to teach that even for her there is no obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second possible author for the משנה: רבי יהודה. It reads the משנה's words to fit his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה the daughter is the stronger case, because feeding her protects her from shame. So if even the daughter has no חובה, the son certainly has none. The מצוה, though, starts with the son and applies to daughters all the more so.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: this introduces another possible answer
And this is what he means: a way of reading the words
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
This is what it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה flip which child is the 'stronger' case. For רבי מאיר the מצוה starts with daughters. For רבי יהודה it starts with sons.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and this is what he is saying:
A father is not obligated in his daughter's sustenance,
and all the more so for his son.
But there is a מצוה regarding his son,
and all the more so for the daughters.
And the fact that it teaches 'his daughter':
it teaches us this:
that even for his daughter there is no obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second author for the משנה instead of רבי מאיר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Matching the משנה to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could only fit רבי מאיר
steps.terutzMaskana: It fits רבי יהודה too: no חובה for either child, with the מצוה running from sons to daughters

steps.title: Third reading: the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can also follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, who holds there is not even a מצוה to feed one's children while alive. The words 'not obligated' were chosen only to match the case of daughters after the father's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא. Read it this way: he is not obligated to feed his daughter, and the same goes for his son. In fact there is not even a מצוה. But since daughters do have an obligation after their father's death, the משנה used the phrase 'not obligated' here too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third possible author: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא. It explains why the משנה says 'not obligated' even though he holds there is no מצוה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading you may not learn 'but there is a מצוה' from the משנה's words. The phrase 'not obligated' is just there to match the case of daughters after the father dies, where there really is a חובה to feed them from his estate. The משנה is setting the two times side by side.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because of: the wording was carried over from another case
He taught: the author of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'not obligated' does NOT hint that there is a מצוה. It is only matching wording, a common move in the גמרא called אַיְּידֵי.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא,
phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka,
and this is what he is saying:
He is not obligated in his daughter's sustenance,
and the same is true for his son.

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ מִצְוָה נָמֵי לֵיכָּא,
phrases.english: And the same is true that there is not even a מצוה,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַיְּידֵי דְּבָנוֹת לְאַחַר מִיתַת אֲבִיהֶן חוֹבָה,
phrases.english: but since for daughters after their father's death it is an obligation,
he also taught 'he is not obligated.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative author for the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the wording as carried over from a matching case (אַיְּידֵי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not obligated' implies there is still a מצוה, which does not fit רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording only matches the after-death case, so the משנה can mean there is not even a מצוה
steps.whatToRemember: Three readings of the משנה: רבי מאיר (מצוה from daughters to sons), רבי יהודה (מצוה from sons to daughters), רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא (no מצוה at all while the father is alive). In all three there is no חובה.

steps.title: The rule made in אושא: a man must feed his young children
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא quotes ריש לקיש, who quotes רבי יהודה בר חנינא: in אושא the חכמים made a rule that a man should feed his sons and daughters while they are minors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said in the name of ריש לקיש, who said it in the name of רבי יהודה בר חנינא: In אושא they made a rule that a person should feed his sons and daughters when they are young.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching. A later rabbinic rule (תקנה) made in אושא requires fathers to feed their young children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, by the משנה's own law there was no חובה to feed children. The תקנת אושא adds a new rabbinic requirement on top of that. It covers sons and daughters alike, but only while they are minors.

keyTerms.meaning: A town in the Galil where the סנהדרין met and made several rules

steps.whyThisMatters: This תקנה moves feeding young children past a mere מצוה. The rest of the סוגיא asks how binding it really is.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said that Reish Lakish said
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Ḥanina:
In Usha they instituted

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהֵא אָדָם זָן אֶת בָּנָיו וְאֶת בְּנוֹתָיו
phrases.english: that a man should feed his sons and his daughters
when they are minors.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a rabbinic rule beyond the משנה's basic law
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים of אושא required a man to feed his young sons and daughters

steps.title: Is the הלכה like the rule of אושא?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask whether the הלכה actually follows this תקנה or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is the הלכה like him, or is the הלכה not like him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about the rule from step 4: do we actually follow it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that a תקנה was made does not settle whether it was accepted in practice. In real life the question is whether בית דין can make a father feed his young children.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים)

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
is the halakha in accordance with him
or is the halakha not in accordance with him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ אוֹ אֵין הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the תקנה from step 4 is followed in practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה follows the תקנת אושא requiring fathers to feed young children

steps.title: רב יהודה's sharp rebuke: even a jackal doesn't dump its young on the town
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story: when people came to רב יהודה about a father who would not feed his children, he would scold the father, comparing him to an animal that leaves its babies for the townspeople to raise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: when people would come before רב יהודה, he would say to them: 'The jackal gives birth and throws them onto the people of the town?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question with a story about how רב יהודה handled a father who would not feed his children. He shamed the father with a sharp comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה uses words of rebuke and shame here; the story does not say he forced the father. This is the first piece of evidence for how binding the תקנה was in practice. The next steps (רב חסדא and רבא) add more evidence.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a source to answer a question
Onto the people of the town

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: When they would come before Rav Yehuda,
phrases.notes: They came to complain about a father who refused to feed his children.

phrases.english: he would say to them:
The jackal gives birth,
and throws them on the townspeople?!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כִּי הֲוָה אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story as evidence to answer the question in step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יהודה rebuked such fathers with shaming words, showing how the duty was treated in practice; steps 7 and 10 add more stories like it

steps.title: רב חסדא publicly shames the father
steps.stepSummary: When such cases came to רב חסדא, he had the father stand on an upside-down mortar in public and announce that even a raven cares for its young, but he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: When people came to רב חסדא, he told them: Turn a mortar over for him in public, and let him stand up and say: 'The raven wants its children, and this man does not want his children!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story, like רב יהודה's, of how a judge handled a father who would not feed his kids. רב חסדא used public shame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב יהודה, רב חסדא pressures the father with words and embarrassment, not by forcing payment. This adds to the picture that the court did not treat the אושא rule as something it could enforce.

keyTerms.meaning: A mortar (a heavy bowl for grinding), flipped over to stand on
In public, in front of the community

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: When they would come before Rav Chisda,
he would say to them:
Turn over a mortar for him in public,
phrases.notes: The upside-down mortar works like a little stage, so everyone can see him.

phrases.english: and let him stand up and say:
The raven wants its children,
and that man does not want his children?!
phrases.notes: 'That man' is the father talking about himself, a way of avoiding saying 'I'.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to רב יהודה's, adding more evidence that the court only shamed the father.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Judges used public shame, not legal force, against a father who would not feed his children.

steps.title: Do ravens really care for their young?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's comparison: a פסוק suggests that young ravens are fed by God because their parents do not feed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does a raven want its children? Isn't it written: 'to the young ravens that cry'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the raven example from the last step, using a פסוק in תהלים that seems to show ravens neglecting their babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says God gives food to the young ravens that cry out. That suggests the parents leave them alone, which is the opposite of what רב חסדא said.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But does a raven want its children?
But isn't it written:
"to the young ravens that cry"!
phrases.notes: תהלים 147:9. God feeds them, which hints that their parents don't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual basis of רב חסדא's comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the raven wants its children
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק describes young ravens crying and being fed by God, implying their parents abandon them.

steps.title: Two kinds of ravens
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction: one statement is about white ravens and the other about black ravens.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is about white ones, and that one is about black ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying different kinds of ravens act differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One type of raven cares for its young, and another type leaves them. So רב חסדא and the פסוק are talking about different ravens, and both are true.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is about white ones,
that is about black ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּחִיוָּרֵי, הָא בְּאוּכָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the raven challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All ravens are the same, so the פסוק contradicts רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two kinds of ravens. One cares for its young and the other does not.

steps.title: רבא asks the father if he's happy with charity
steps.stepSummary: When such a case came to רבא, he asked the father whether he was comfortable having his children fed by charity.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a case came before רבא, he would say to the father: Are you happy that your children are fed from charity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third story of a judge handling a father who would not feed his kids. רבא used a sharp question to make him feel ashamed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the judge only presses with words. Taken together, these stories answer the question from step 5: the court did not force the father, so the הלכה does not follow the אושא rule as an enforced duty.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it pleasing to you? Are you okay with it?

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה, רב חסדא and רבא all shamed the father but did not force him. This shows the court did not enforce the אושא rule for feeding young children.

phrases.english: When such a case would come before Rava,
he would say to him:
Are you happy
that your children are fed from charity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the raven side point to the series of stories about judges.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The judge used shame, not force, which shows the הלכה does not follow the אושא rule as a legal duty.

steps.title: A wealthy father can be forced
steps.stepSummary: The rule that we don't force the father applies only when he is not wealthy. If he is wealthy, the court forces him to feed his children.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he is not wealthy. But if he is wealthy, we force him against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a limit on what it just showed. 'No forcing' applies only to a father who is not wealthy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor father who struggles is only shamed. A wealthy father is forced to support his children, even though no special duty from the אושא rule applies.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this (in a limited case)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the court never forces a father. The stories of shaming are about a father who is not wealthy. A wealthy father is forced.

phrases.english: And we only said this
when he is not wealthy,
but if he is wealthy,
we force him against his will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the conclusion of the stories to a father who is not wealthy.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A father who is not wealthy is only shamed into feeding his young children. A wealthy father is forced by the court.

steps.title: רבא forced a rich man to give charity
steps.stepSummary: Support: רבא forced the wealthy רב נתן בר אמי to give four hundred זוז to charity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this case: רבא forced רב נתן בר אמי and took four hundred זוז from him for charity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to support the rule that a wealthy person can be forced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the court can force a rich man to give charity to strangers, it can surely force a rich father to feed his own children.

phrases.english: Like this case of Rava,
who forced Rav Natan bar Ami
and took from him
four hundred zuz for charity.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרָבָא כַּפְיֵיהּ לְרַב נָתָן בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a case to support the rule that a wealthy person is forced.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a wealthy father can be forced
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא forcing רב נתן בר אמי to give 400 זוז to charity

steps.title: A father who gives everything to his sons is still supported
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא quotes ריש לקיש: in אושא they decreed that a man who gives all his property to his sons is still supported from it, together with his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said in the name of ריש לקיש: In אושא they decreed that if someone writes over all his property to his sons, he and his wife are fed from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a second rule made in אושא. This one protects parents who hand over all their property to their children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the property now belongs to the sons, the father and his wife still get their food from it. This is a new rule, separate from the earlier אושא rule about feeding young children.

keyTerms.meaning: אושא, the town where the חכמים made several rules

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said that Reish Lakish said:
In Usha they decreed:
one who writes over all his property to his sons,
he and his wife are fed from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: בְּאוּשָׁא הִתְקִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same רבי אילעא / ריש לקיש chain as step 4, this time without רבי יהודה בר חנינא, to bring a new אושא rule on a different topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who gives all his property to his sons is still supported from it, together with his wife.

steps.title: Why was this rule needed? A bigger rule already exists
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, or some say רבי שמואל בר נחמני, challenges the תקנה of אושא. חז״ל already said that a widow is fed from her husband's property even after it passed out of the heir's hands (the next steps give the source), which is a much bigger חידוש. So why state that a living man and his wife are fed from property he gave his sons?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objects to this, and some say it was רבי שמואל בר נחמני: They said something even greater than this, that his widow is fed from his property! Do we really need to be told about him and his wife?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the תקנה of אושא from Step 13. It says the rule is obvious, because חז״ל already said something more extreme.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is a 'how much more so' argument. If even a widow is fed from her husband's property after it has left the family, then a living man is surely fed from property he himself gave away. The full source for 'the greater thing' comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it; he challenges the statement
And some say; the statement is said in another person's name
They said something even greater than this, a bigger חידוש
Is it necessary? Used to say something is obvious

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objects to it
and some say it was Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani:
They said something greater than this,
phrases.notes: 'Greater' here means a more surprising ruling, one that goes further than the אושא rule.

phrases.english: his widow is fed from his property,
so is it necessary to say this about him and his wife?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the תקנה of אושא stated in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The תקנה of אושא that a man who gave his property to his sons is fed from it together with his wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case can be learned by קל וחומר from the widow, so the תקנה seems unnecessary

steps.title: The source: רבין's letter about the widow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source for the 'greater thing.' רבין sent a letter saying that a widow is fed from her husband's property, and this stays true even after the daughter who inherited him gets married.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבין sent in his letter: If a man died and left a widow and a daughter, his widow is fed from his property. If the daughter married, his widow is still fed from his property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the 'greater thing' from Step 14 comes from. It quotes רבין's letter about a widow and a daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter is the heir. Once she marries, her husband controls the property. Even so, the widow keeps her right to be fed from it, which shows how strong that right is.

phrases.english: For Ravin sent in his letter:
One who died and left a widow and a daughter
his widow is fed from his property.
If the daughter got married
his widow is still fed from his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the 'greater thing' mentioned in Step 14
steps.raayaObject: That a widow's right to be fed from her husband's property is very strong

steps.title: Even after the daughter dies, the widow is fed
steps.stepSummary: רבין's letter goes further. Even if the daughter died, רבי יהודה, the nephew of רבי יוסי בר חנינא, reports that he was involved in such a case, and the ruling was that the widow is still fed from the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the daughter died, רבי יהודה, the son of the sister of רבי יוסי בר חנינא, said: There was such a case through me, and they ruled that his widow is fed from his property.
steps.whatsHappening: The letter adds the most extreme case. Even when the daughter has died, the widow is still fed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the daughter dies, the property has moved even further from the original family. A real case came before the חכמים, and they still ruled for the widow. This is the full 'greater thing' that רבי זירא is pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: A case happened through me; I was involved in it

phrases.english: If the daughter died,
Rabbi Yehuda, the son of the sister
of Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina, said:
There was such a case through me,
and they said: His widow is fed from his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבין's letter with the most extreme case
steps.raayaObject: That the widow is fed even after the daughter who inherited has died
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case reported by רבי יהודה, nephew of רבי יוסי בר חנינא

steps.title: So surely a living man and his wife are fed
steps.stepSummary: With the full source laid out, the גמרא repeats its challenge. If the widow is fed even in such far-removed cases, why do we need the תקנה of אושא for a living man and his wife?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it necessary to say this about him and his wife?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the question from Step 14, now that the proof is complete. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added. The repetition closes the proof and puts the question back on the table: the אושא rule still seems obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: He and his wife, meaning the father who gave his property away

phrases.english: Is it necessary to say this about him and his wife?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge of Step 14 after the source has been fully quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the תקנה of אושא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר from the widow's case

steps.title: A living husband can work, so the תקנה was needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the widow case does not prove the father's case. A widow is fed because she has nobody to work for her. A living husband can work for himself and his wife, so we might have said he must go earn a living. The תקנה teaches that he does not have to.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: There, with the widow, the rule applies because there is nobody to work for her. But here, the husband can work for himself and for her. So the תקנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows a real difference between the widow and the living husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר fails because the widow has a special reason to be fed: she is alone, and nobody can work for her. The husband can still work, so we might have thought he should support himself and his wife by his own effort. The תקנה of אושא tells us he may still be fed from the property he gave his sons.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces a mistaken idea the rule comes to correct
To work hard, to make the effort to earn
There / here; contrasts the two cases

steps.whatToRemember: The תקנה of אושא is not obvious. A widow is fed because nobody can work for her. A living husband could work, but the תקנה says he and his wife are still fed from the property he gave his sons.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'let him work for himself and for her' is the mistaken idea, not the conclusion. The conclusion (קא משמע לן) is that he does NOT have to work; he is fed from the property.

phrases.english: You might have said:
there, the rule applies because there is nobody to work for her,
but here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the living father who gave his property to his sons.

phrases.english: let him work for himself and for her,
so it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 14 and 17 by showing a difference between the cases
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases (חילוק): a widow cannot work, but a living husband can
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A living husband should have to work to support himself and his wife instead of drawing on the property
steps.terutzMaskana: The תקנה of אושא teaches that he and his wife are fed from the property even though he could work

steps.title: Do we rule like the תקנה of אושא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the הלכה follows רבי אילעא's report of the תקנה of אושא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars asked: Is the הלכה like him, or is the הלכה not like him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has finished explaining why the תקנה was needed. Now it asks a practical question: do we actually rule this way?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about why the תקנה was needed at all. Knowing a ruling's reason does not tell us whether the final הלכה follows it. So the גמרא asks for the practical bottom line.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars
The הלכה does not follow it

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Is the halacha like him
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי אילעא, the one who reported the תקנה of אושא about a man who writes his property to his sons.

phrases.english: or is the halacha not like him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining why the תקנה was needed to asking whether we rule like it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the practical halacha follows רבי אילעא's report of the תקנה of אושא.

steps.title: A man kisses רבי יונתן's foot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a story to answer the question: a man bowed down and kissed רבי יונתן's foot while he stood with רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי חנינא and רבי יונתן were standing together. A certain man came, bent down, and kissed רבי יונתן on his foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that will answer the question. Right now it is only setting the scene for the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kissing someone's foot is an unusual act of deep thanks. The story makes us ask what רבי יונתן did for this man. That answer will connect the story to the תקנה of אושא.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to answer

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן הֲווֹ קָיְימִי,
phrases.english: For Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Yonatan were standing,
a certain man came
bent down and kissed Rabbi Yonatan on his foot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story brought as evidence to answer the question of step 19.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the halacha follows the תקנה of אושא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about רבי יונתן and a grateful man, told in front of רבי חנינא.

steps.title: רבי יונתן starts to explain the kiss
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא asks what this was about. רבי יונתן begins to explain that the man had written his property over to his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said to him: What is this? He said to him: He is someone who wrote his property over to his sons,
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא asks why the man kissed רבי יונתן's foot. רבי יונתן starts to explain, and his answer continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we see the link: this man is exactly the case of the תקנה of אושא, someone who wrote his property to his sons. How רבי יונתן helped him will show how the תקנה was applied in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? Why is this happening?
One who writes his property over to his sons

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי הַאי?
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said to him: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כּוֹתֵב נְכָסָיו לְבָנָיו הוּא,
phrases.english: He said to him: He is one who wrote his property to his sons,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the story's scene and shows that the man is exactly the case of the תקנה of אושא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the halacha follows the תקנה of אושא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יונתן's explanation of the man's case, which continues in the next lines.
